content: Panthenol is the alcohol derivative of pantothenic acid, also known as vitamin B5, and serves as its provitamin. Within living organisms, it is rapidly oxidized to pantothenate. At room temperature, panthenol exists as a highly viscous, transparent liquid. In contrast, salts of pantothenic acid, such as sodium pantothenate, are typically white powders. Panthenol is highly soluble in water, alcohol, and propylene glycol, moderately soluble in ether and chloroform, and only slightly soluble in glycerin. Panthenol exists in two enantiomeric forms: D-panthenol and L-panthenol. Of these, only D-panthenol, also referred to as dexpanthenol, is biologically active. However, both enantiomers exhibit moisturizing properties. For cosmetic applications, panthenol is available either as the D-form or as a racemic mixture containing both Dand L-panthenol (DL-panthenol). The chemical structure of panthenol is represented as HO-CH2-C(CH3)2-CH(OH)-CONH-CH2CH2CH2-OH. In the field of cosmetics, panthenol functions as a humectant, emollient, and moisturizer. It has a strong affinity for binding to hair follicles and is commonly included in shampoos and hair conditioners at concentrations ranging from 0.1% to 1%. When applied to hair, it forms a coating that seals the surface of the strands, providing lubrication to the follicles and imparting a shiny appearance to the hair. In topical ointments, panthenol is often combined with allantoin in concentrations of 2% to 5%. These formulations are used to treat sunburns, minor burns, and mild skin conditions. However, panthenol is not absorbed through the skin, and its effects are limited to its surface activity rather than its role as a provitamin. When ingested, panthenol is metabolized into pantothenic acid. Panthenol is also known by several alternative names, including: Butanamide, 2,4-dihydroxy-N-(3-hydroxypropyl)-3,3-dimethyl-, (R)Butyramide, 2,4-dihydroxy-N-(3-hydroxypropyl)-3,3-dimethyl-, D-(+)Butanamide, 2,4-dihydroxy-N-(3-hydroxypropyl)-3,3-dimethyl-, (2R)D-Panthenol Dexpanthenol (DCIR) Dexpanthenolum Propanolamine, N-pantoyld-Pantothenyl alcohol
